channel.title: Long Way Round
channel.description: slow stories from Irad, written to be read to the end

item.title: A note before leaving
item.description: I am starting at a newspaper in Talas. A few lines about what these long pages were for. [photo: river | The Talas in March, still grey.] Three years, six long stories, about 4,000 readers. Two of the stories were reprinted in the Talas Herald, one was read on the radio. The projectionist's son…

item.title: The bus to the end of the line
item.description: The village bus runs from the Talas bazaar to the last village before the hills. Two hours, forty stops, and a driver who knows every passenger's mother. [photo: bus | The village bus at the final stop, waiting.] The driver, Asylbek, has driven this route for fourteen years. He does not need to…

item.title: Night shift at the boiler house
item.description: In every block of flats in Nurzhan someone keeps the heat on. A night with the stokers of a district boiler house. [photo: night | The boiler house chimney at 2 a.m.] The boiler house heats eleven blocks. Inside it is 34 degrees and loud like the inside of a drum. The three men of the night shift…

item.title: The house of culture that never closed
item.description: In the Kara-Buura district a Soviet house of culture still hosts a komuz ensemble every Thursday. Nobody has paid for the heating since 1998. [photo: town | The House of Culture in the district centre, February.] The building has a portico with four columns, a mosaic of a tractor and a harvest,…

item.title: Three buckets an hour
item.description: In July the road to Iyık Janyl becomes a market. A day with the families who pick, sort and sell the apricots. [photo: apricots | The Kalys family's trees at 6 a.m.] The pickers start at five, before the sun reaches the orchard. Gulnara Kalys, 52, works with her daughters and two nieces on…

item.title: The last projectionist
item.description: For forty years Bakyt Mamatov showed films to Talas. Then the films stopped coming, and he kept the projector oiled anyway. [photo: night | The old cinema on a weekday evening. The sign still lights up, half of it.] The cinema opened in 1967 with an Indian film, and Bakyt Mamatov, then nineteen,…
